clue.text: Harmony on a C string

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a cord is a thin string

explanation.surface: A musician praises the sweet harmony produced on the C string of a cello.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'C string' look like one item, but A, C and a string are three separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Accord means agreement or concord, a close synonym of harmony between people.

clue.text: Team from Cheshire town's incomplete

indicators.note: something incomplete is missing a part, here its final letter

parts.note: Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England

explanation.surface: A sports side drawn from a Cheshire town cannot field a full eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last E from the town's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a group of people working together, such as a rowing or ship's team.

clue.text: Involved boys in act of perversity

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some lads were caught up in a deliberately contrary piece of behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinacy is stubborn contrariness, the wilful refusal to do what is reasonable, which is perversity.

clue.text: In Scotland, do not go to supper!

indicators.note: a Scottish speaker's pronunciation of the phrase is what the solver must listen to

parts.note: dinna is Scots for do not, and said in a Scottish accent it sounds like the evening meal

explanation.surface: A Scottish host warns a guest not to come for the evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun relies on the Scots form dinna (as in 'dinna fash') sounding like the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper and dinner are both names for the main evening meal, used interchangeably in much of Britain.

clue.text: Average pupil can be confused by English jargon

parts.note: par is the normal or average level

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled out of their order

parts.note: L for learner, a pupil
taken as written, to be rearranged
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An ordinary student may be baffled by the technical vocabulary of English studies.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of speaking, especially the specialised vocabulary of a group, which is jargon.

clue.text: Upset teetotaller when drunken horde went to celebrate wildly

parts.note: to upset someone is to pain them

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering about, so these letters lurch into a new arrangement

parts.note: TT is the standard abbreviation for teetotal
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A non-drinker is dismayed when a drunken mob goes out partying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset teetotaller' reads as one phrase, but upset is a verb meaning pain, and the teetotaller is just TT.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint the town red is an idiom for going out and celebrating in a noisy, extravagant way.

clue.text: Criticising cooking method?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: cooking food in an oven with dry heat

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the cooking sense is also slang for a dressing-down.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both harsh rebuking of someone and baking meat or vegetables in an oven.

clue.text: Room high-up over Italian city

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned over, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: città is the Italian word for city

explanation.surface: A garret perched above an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian city' looks like it wants a place name such as Rome, but it is the Italian word for city.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the space or room just under the roof of a house, the highest room in it.

clue.text: Company has top management pledge to arbitrate

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of management
a pledge is a promise

explanation.surface: A firm's senior managers promise to settle a dispute between staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise once meant to settle a dispute by mutual concession or arbitration, which is to arbitrate.

clue.text: City man left on short skiing trip

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters fall into a new order
short means cut off, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written, to be cut and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man departs on a brief ski holiday to a northern capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skiing trip' looks like a holiday, but trip tells you to jumble the shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital of Finland, and so a city.

clue.text: Fall back in sudden mutual surprise

indicators.note: back means read from right to left
in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and most of the second

explanation.surface: Two people both start back in shock at the same moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall back' suggests retreat, but Fall is the definition and back is the reversal signal; surprise is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall is the North American name for the season between summer and winter, autumn.

clue.text: Being in CID possibly a way to prove myself

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other, splitting the outer one

parts.note: CID could stand for card ID, which is an ID card
an entity is a being

explanation.surface: Someone serving with the detective branch needs papers to prove who they are.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, but 'possibly' lets the initials stand for something else entirely, an identity document.
explanation.definitionFit: An identity card is an official document carried to show who you are, so it proves one's own identity.

clue.text: Unwilling to accept translated Oriental books

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A reader refuses to take on Eastern texts in translation.
explanation.definitionFit: Intolerant describes someone who will not accept views, people or conditions different from their own.

clue.text: A two-faced girl

parts.note: surface reading: a deceitful, hypocritical young woman
setter's reading: a girl's name that faces the same way both ways, reading identically forwards and backwards

explanation.walkthrough: Two-faced normally means insincere; here it describes a name that is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a female first name that is spelt the same in either direction, so it has two matching faces.

clue.text: Worker's a bit gorgeous!

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
some means a bit, a certain amount

explanation.surface: An admiring remark that a labourer is rather attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome means good-looking, a near synonym of gorgeous when said of a person.

clue.text: The French National Front Party's wrapped up in drive for glory

indicators.note: wrapped up in means enclosed by, so these letters go inside the outer word

parts.note: to spur is to drive on
le is French for the

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of National
a do is a party

explanation.surface: France's National Front party is absorbed in its campaign for glory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National Front' looks like the far-right party; here Front just takes the first letter of National.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is magnificent grandeur or brilliance, a sense close to glory.

clue.text: Band supporter allowed to go after church

indicators.note: going after places this piece later in the sequence than the other

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
CE is the Church of England
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A music group's fan is permitted to leave once the church service ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Band and supporter suggest a pop group and its fan; the supporter is a bra.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is a decorative band worn around the wrist.

clue.text: Good book, worthily produced!

indicators.note: produced means made up or fashioned, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine novel that has been published with real merit.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy writ is sacred scripture, the Bible, which is often called the Good Book.

clue.text: Stroke put son in Los Angeles hospital

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: LA is the usual abbreviation for Los Angeles
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: After a stroke, a man's son was admitted to a hospital in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: Stroke wants to be the medical event, but it is a blow with a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A lash is a single stroke of a whip, the blow delivered by it.

clue.text: I myself keep parking down by East Block

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside

parts.note: me refers to myself
P is the sign for parking
D is the abbreviation for down
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Someone insists on keeping their own parking spot down beside the East Block.
explanation.walkthrough: East Block reads like a building; Block is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To impede is to obstruct or hinder progress, which is to block.

clue.text: Forces girl to get work with Arab country

parts.note: service is work done for others
W is an abbreviation for with
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A girl is compelled to take a job in a Gulf state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forces' reads as a verb, compels; it is the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A servicewoman is a female member of the armed forces.

clue.text: Reluctant to miss beginning of poem

indicators.note: missing the beginning means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: averse means unwilling or reluctant

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to skip the opening lines of a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is writing arranged in metrical lines, and a verse can be a short poem.

clue.text: Works, having married badly

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for married
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: It works, even though the marriage went badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Works looks like a verb; it is a noun, a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill is a factory or industrial plant, and works is another word for such a place.

clue.text: Police hit by job cut

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a pat is a light hit
a role is a job or function

explanation.surface: The police force suffers from job losses.
explanation.walkthrough: Police is a verb here, to keep watch over an area.
explanation.definitionFit: To patrol is to go round an area keeping watch, which is to police it.

clue.text: Roman Catholic embracing new theories loses two points for verbosity …

indicators.note: embracing means holding around, so the outer letters enclose the rest

parts.note: RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh order
points are compass directions, and two of them are to be removed

parts.note: taken as written, to lose S and E and be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Catholic who takes up novel ideas loses marks for being wordy.
explanation.walkthrough: The two compass points dropped from the theories are S and E; the ellipsis links this clue to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric can mean language that is elaborate and showy but empty, which amounts to verbosity.

clue.text: … clearly evidenced at trial of French revolutionary

parts.note: taken as written
a test is a trial

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: de is French for of

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: facts proved at the trial of a French revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French revolutionary' suggests Robespierre; here revolutionary turns round the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Attested means proved or borne witness to, so clearly evidenced.

clue.text: In a strange way, anger's overcome in cathedral

indicators.note: in places this piece inside the other word

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: overcome suggests being turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Fury strangely subsides inside a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerily means in an uncanny, unsettling manner, which is a strange way.
